```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Transportation_Problem")
    m.setParam("TimeLimit", 100)  # Set time limit to 100 seconds

    # Data
    sources = list(range(10))  # S0..S9
    destinations = list(range(12))  # D0..D11

    supplies = [15, 27, 48, 32, 12, 56, 22, 34, 33, 53]
    demands = [15, 18, 16, 26, 16, 24, 15, 22, 24, 29, 22, 8]

    # Cost matrix: rows correspond to sources S0..S9, columns to destinations D0..D11
    costs = [
        [  9.53,  15.53,  23.04,  12.82,   5.10,  24.68,   9.26,  16.93,  20.17,  19.66,  20.95,  29.46],  # S0
        [ 12.96,  16.87,   9.71,   8.64,  18.51,  21.81,  28.90,  27.24,   6.75,  15.75,  22.80,  18.03],  # S1
        [  8.63,   9.59,  27.74,  23.26,  11.42,  12.07,  26.10,  29.41,  22.88,   9.15,  28.25,  10.99],  # S2
        [ 13.58,  22.03,   9.40,  28.05,   9.28,  21.35,  14.09,   8.99,  27.92,  14.01,  17.60,   6.91],  # S3
        [ 15.29,   5.92,  16.74,  13.80,   7.43,  22.95,  22.56,   5.75,  12.28,  19.22,   7.25,   6.24],  # S4
        [ 28.78,  23.06,  15.25,  25.67,  22.38,  12.53,  11.96,  23.00,  23.59,   6.20,  16.11,  29.17],  # S5
        [ 25.62,  28.05,  19.76,  13.13,  27.01,  24.63,   7.89,  22.99,  14.53,  18.15,  16.98,   5.34],  # S6
        [  7.98,  11.33,  10.30,  23.65,  21.31,  25.81,   5.77,  22.02,  17.55,   6.63,   5.10,  25.04],  # S7
        [ 22.81,  22.48,  26.66,  22.10,  17.19,  12.95,   8.22,  11.22,  20.04,  13.33,  16.15,  27.56],  # S8
        [ 20.59,  20.52,  29.78,  10.03,   6.99,  17.92,  11.87,  21.19,  14.42,  19.37,  17.78,  10.02],  # S9
    ]

    # Decision variables:
    # Flow_S{i}_D{j} >= 0 is the quantity shipped from source i to destination j
    flows = {}
    for i in sources:
        for j in destinations:
            flows[(i, j)] = m.addVar(lb=0.0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name=f"Flow_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Objective: Minimize total transportation cost
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(costs[i][j] * flows[(i, j)] for i in sources for j in destinations),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # Supply constraints: Shipments from each source <= its supply
    for i in sources:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for j in destinations) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}"
        )

    # Demand constraints: Shipments to each destination >= its demand
    for j in destinations:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(flows[(i, j)] for i in sources) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}"
        )

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Operations and Finance Leadership  
From: Supply Chain Director  
Date: [Insert Date]  
Subject: Network shipping plan to meet demand at lowest total freight cost

Situation
We operate a network of source locations (warehouses and factories) that must supply a set of destination locations (stores, customers, and regional hubs). Lane rates vary across routes, and available inventory differs by site. A deliberate shipping plan is needed to control freight spend, protect margins, and uphold service levels. Shipments must be planned in whole units (e.g., full pallets or truckloads); partial loads are not allowed.

Problem
We need a clear, feasible plan that assigns shipments from each source to each destination so that:
- No source ships more than its available inventory or throughput limits.
- Every destination receives its full required quantity.
- All shipments are planned in whole-unit increments only.
- The overall combination of routes results in the lowest achievable total shipping cost without compromising service.

In practical terms, the challenge is to balance supply availability, destination needs, and lane costs across our network. Some routes are cheaper but may have limited supply at the origin; others are more expensive but closer to the demand point. The plan must align with our service commitments and staging schedules, with attention to carrier capacity and loading constraints associated with whole-unit moves.

Approach and next steps
- Confirm the current supply position at each source, the required quantities by destination, and the route-level shipping costs (see Annex).
- Validate operational assumptions: unit of measure for whole loads, loading windows, carrier availability, and any routing restrictions.
- Produce a lane-by-lane allocation that specifies how many whole units move from each source to each destination.
- Review the recommended plan with Operations and Finance to confirm feasibility, expected service performance, and projected freight spend.
- Finalize execution instructions for sites and carriers, including any exceptions or contingency routes.

The outcome will be a transparent shipping plan that meets all requirements at the lowest total freight cost, with clear guidance for execution in the field.
